title: RT by @markjeffrey: No, it definitely won't. I personally spent several years building SHA-256 as a Boolean circuit and then using all the most sophisticated techniques known to math and cryptography to try to invert that function (to execute a preimage attack). I know the math of SHA-256 more deeply than most people on this planet. It's exceptionally well-defined as a trapdoor function, and inverting it is most certainly NP complete. I also spent over 30 years trying to prove that P = NP, and threw my entire 30 years of knowledge of this problem at frontier LLMs to try to crack it. What they ended up doing was to thoroughly and convincingly refute every single line of reasoning and "clever" trick I came up with over those decades, which has now left me believing for the first time that actually P≠NP.

name: Pantera Capital
title: RT by @PanteraCapital: Just wrapped Money20/20. My biggest takeaway as a VC: the two forces reshaping fintech right now are AI agents and stablecoins. @SirDigitalDan from @CoinflowLabs and I dug into both in our fireside. Some takeaways: * Where will value accrue? AI is collapsing the cost of cognition, and stablecoins the cost of settlement. This changes value accrual, when those inputs aren’t scarce. I’m expecting value to migrate to regulated trust, proprietary data, distribution, underlying physical assets, networks. * What does stablecoins as programmable money unlock? Funds and spending rules can execute together, letting a product enforce agent budgets or trigger conditional payouts with less coordination across banks, processors and operational teams. * Where is agent demand emerging? Dan pointed to compute, inference and data APIs, which agents need to complete tasks. I’m looking for infra on fraud, KYA, chargebacks, and merchant side ops to help proliferate agentic commerce usage. * Who carries agent liability? A purchase can comply with the spending rules and still be a mistake. Before delegating larger budgets, businesses will want audit trails, a way to dispute purchases and an agreement on who absorbs losses. * Where’s the distribution advantage? Local integrations and merchant relationships give providers access to existing payment volume. Stablecoins can improve settlement without changing how customers pay. (Coinflow connects cards, ACH and PIX this way.) * How do existing PSPs participate? A provider can earn a processing fee when a developer funds an agent by card, even if subsequent payments settle in stablecoins. (Coinflow powers card funding for Tempo’s MPP Credits.) Thanks for the week @money2020! Curious what others took away too!

title: Here's a very crude simplified chutes roadmap/plan, for near term: - move the most unprofitable things off of the subnet, including today's announcement of some (not all) additional inference options (not paid via emissions) - this allows us to scale the things we want and need to avoid capacity issues/better direct incentive - this includes models we use to build data pipelines and relationships to other teams/networks/etc - add options that are completely revenue positive (hourly pricing/rentals/simple docker based jobs/etc), TEE, private, secure, priced above cost, more extensive version of private chutes we have today basically - expand the hourly compute offerings to also include CPU only (e.g. to run agents, web browsers, sandboxes, non-GPU work of any kind) - use some of the incentive for ideally non-datacenter based model training and serving - build a non-extractable product on chutes from the models we build, via dynamic edge nodes, possibly from the epigenesis work (smaller faster cheaper faster than lora customizations from the sparse sections of pretrained model, participant supplied) - models and pipeline etc. will be open source, the customization and ensemble thereof will live only in chutes, inc. the continuously evolving set of served variations/RL/etc. We'd like, to the extent we can, attract participants who want to build and have no obligation to pay datacenters or any particular hardware vendor, to keep the value inside the subnet at all times by attacking sell pressure at the source (DC commitments, chip purchases, etc). We will continue to have secure TEE inference and GPUs; not elimating anything wholesale, just focusing more on a commodity that doesn't have to flow out to DCs and single hardware vendors. NVIDIA reportedly has 75% profit margins, revenue for the sake of revenue fueling GPU reselling goes straight to one place, basically. Fine, I guess, but I'd rather work together as individuals with whatever hardware we can bring, to a reasonable degree.

title: True? No clue. The point of parallax is to put the network into as many hands as possible in a verifiable trustless way, and for the output (the models) to not require yet another source for the wealthiest companies on earth to monopolize (that is, a model that can run even on a phone and not require "now's" completely unaffordable mega GPU). The current AI marketplace is fueled by a massive debt market with very few beneficiaries at the world's expense. If you like K shaped economies here it is in plain sight; trickle up resources, consolidating into a few, spreading the gap at ever-increasing speed. Whether this is self serving for Mr. Musk to gather up more resources for pennies on the dollar or a true statement is irrelevant, the outcome is the same. Will it crash tomorrow, next week, never? No clue, but I would rather not build the foundation on this gamble. I'm possibly (probably?) doing it wrong, but the goal is and has always been, people first, which means accessibility first. Let's make "good enough" models with no kill switch and no hardware moat. Please and thank you. If we get superintelligence out into the universe without/at the cost of consciousness to witness it, we have accomplished nothing, and have in fact forgotten the whole point.
